pr_body:
This commit modifies the "elasticsearch-certutil cert" command to add a verify step after the generation of the new certificate.

The primary purpose of this verify is to ensure that the key used to sign the certificate matches the issuing certificate that was provided. That is, if the CA is provided using PEM files, that the `--ca-cert` and `--ca-key` are a matching pair.

There are more efficient ways to tell is a certificate and key are a matching pair if you know what type of key is being used (RSA, EC, etc) but post-signing verification is the most straight-forward way to perform a key-type agnostic check, and is a useful general purpose check to include in certificate generation.

Closes: #98207

issue_context.title: Elastic certutil generates certificates even though the provided ca-key does not match the ca-certificates
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.8.1

### Installed Plugins

_No response_

### Java Version

_bundled_

### OS Version

Linux LAPTOP-85G6IQGC 5.15.90.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP Fri Jan 27 02:56:13 UTC 2023 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Problem Description

Elasticsearch Certutil generates certificates (which are invalid) when the provided ca.key does not match the ca.crt. The expected behavior is that no certificates are generated and that the tool exit with an error clearly saying that ca.key does not match ca.crt. Similarly to what does openssl already.



### Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate two new CA key-certificate pairs:
  - `./bin/elasticsearch-certutil ca --ca-dn "CN=A" --keysize 4096 --pem --out A.zip`
  - `./bin/elasticsearch-certutil ca --ca-dn "CN=B" --keysize 4096 --pem --out B.zip`
2. Unzip the files
  - `unzip A.zip -d A`
  - `unzip B.zip -d B`
3. Generate a certificate by using the ca.crt of A and the ca.key of B:
  - `./bin/elasticsearch-certutil cert --ca-cert ./A/ca/ca.crt --ca-key ./B/ca.key --dns=test.it --pem --name test.it --out testit.zip`
4. Unzip the certificate
  - `unzip testit.zip`
5. Check that the certificate is not valid:
  - `openssl verify -CAfile ../certs/caA/ca.crt ./test.it.crt`


The result is:

> error 7 at 0 depth lookup: certificate signature failure
error ./test.it.crt: verification failed
80CB474EA67F0000:error:0200008A:rsa routines:RSA_padding_check_PKCS1_type_1:invalid padding:../crypto/rsa/rsa_pk1.c:75:
80CB474EA67F0000:error:02000072:rsa routines:rsa_ossl_public_decrypt:padding check failed:../crypto/rsa/rsa_ossl.c:598:
80CB474EA67F0000:error:1C880004:Provider routines:rsa_verify:RSA lib:../providers/implementations/signature/rsa_sig.c:774:
80CB474EA67F0000:error:06880006:asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_item_verify_ctx:EVP lib:../crypto/asn1/a_verify.c:217:


Trying to do the same with openssl results as expected in an error:

`openssl req -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -keyout key.pem -x509 -out ./certificate.pem -CA ./certs/A/ca/ca.crt -CAkey ./certs/caB/ca.key`

> Issuer CA certificate and key do not match
806BE8552B7F0000:error:05800074:x509 certificate routines:X509_check_private_key:key values mismatch:../crypto/x509/x509_cmp.c:405:


### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

review_comments:
This test fails for me when a randomly generated password is larger than 50 chars:
https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/7qquwban7ymjw

Reproduce with:
```
./gradlew ':x-pack:plugin:security:cli:test' --tests "org.elasticsearch.xpack.security.cli.CertificateToolTests.testErrorIfSigningCertificateAndKeyDontMatch" -Dtests.seed=8DE86CB48F6EC3DF -Dtests.locale=es-CL -Dtests.timezone=Etc/GMT-4 -Druntime.java=21
```

I took a closer look and the problem is with calling `generateCA` method twice. It fails in case when the first call creates a password larger than 50 chars and the second call doesn't. The terminal will contain the output of both commands and assertion in the second call will fail. The easiest solution is to simply call `terminal.reset();` after first `generateCA` call.
Thanks - that made the fix much easier.
